text: {"score":3,"justification":"The core numbers match the card and tool outputs, and the summary correctly fixes the draft's error about the audit trail. It also notes that the charts largely support the billed level and that recovery should wait for a coder re-score. But the text contradicts itself, the cited examples fit their points poorly, and the next steps are weakly targeted, so an investigator would have to redo some of the analysis.","problems":["The headline asserts 'notes look inflated, with audit-trail signs' and the rationale says 'This fits notes written up to match the bill'. This is stronger than the evidence supports: the tool output says these are baseline-type rates, not proof, and the charts support the billed level (0 of 13 99215s below billed). Cautious wording such as 'not a finding' was dropped.","The leaning is 'pattern_consistent_with_upcoding' while the summary also says the charts support the billed level and the overpayment estimate is small. This tension is not reconciled. The estimate figures ($449, CI 0-1188) are not given, only 'small'.","Several rationale sentences repeat themselves (the 5 of 22 no-test-line finding and the 57% problems finding each appear twice). The rationale also has meta-commentary ('The draft summary says no audit trail was received; that is wrong'), which is useless to an investigator and reads as internal drafting residue.","The 37% duplicates figure is not in the displayed note-check line and is not explained. The 'problems' sign is not defined, so it is unclear what '57% address fewer problems' means.","The cited examples do not match the argument. C0068352 is a 99214 below billed, and it is the only below-billed chart. C0068179, C0068185 and C0068200 are low-complexity 99215s, but none of them is shown to have a problem in the records. The claims flagged by note_checks (e.g. C0068295, C0068367, C0068375) are not cited. C0068375 is also a low-complexity 99215 that was flagged late, bulk-created and paste-heavy, so it would have been the better example.","The audit-trail request step asks for the trail on the same three claims that were already received in round 2. It is redundant, and the summary does not say that the trail was already received. The sampling-plan step also says to review a random sample after noting that the existing sample was already random (kind random), which makes it confusing.","Documented supported 99215s with high MDM and 40-49 minutes (e.g. C0068246, which is also a low-complexity claim) are not mentioned. This counter-evidence weakens the picture of low-complexity patients.","The MISSING_RESULTS deficiency in the records exchange is not flagged as a gap."]}
